page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Margin notes stand in the left margin, beside the lines "adiudicauit," and "Cuius rei causa". Running head at the top, with the page number 18 at the left.

main_text.p: si apud populum Rom. audi tum est? Facile ut appareat uerisimum esse, quod Cicero nō uno loco prædicat: Romanos omnia consequi potuisse, simul ut uelle cœperant. Præclare igitur sapientissimus poeta, qui cum suas cuique genti laudes attribuisset, pingēdi, sculpendi, obseruandi cœli: Romanis Reipublicæ constituendæ scientiā adiudicauit,Tu regere, inquit, imperio populos Romane memento:Hæ tibi erunt artes, paciq; imponere morem.
Cuius rei causa quæ tandē esse potuerit, cum apud me considero, hanc ferè reperio præcipuam fuisse, quòd cùm nulla

page.notes: The header is partly unreadable; the decorated caps after "II." could not be read and are marked as illegible. The left-margin verse lines are read from the scan with some doubt about which words are italic. The page appears to be a fragment: the first line continues from the previous page, and the last line runs on to the next page.
